title: Funeral Welcome Sign Template: What to Include, Sizes & Printing
description: Create a gentle entrance for the service. Learn what to write on a funeral welcome sign, standard sizes, and how to print a matching template today.
h1: Funeral Welcome Sign Template: What to Include, Sizes & Printing
intro: A welcome sign sets a gentle tone as guests arrive. This guide covers what to write, which sizes work for easels or foam-board mounting, and how to personalize and print a matching template in minutes using free software.

sections.h2: What is a funeral welcome sign and why use one?
paragraphs: A funeral welcome sign sits at the entrance of the service venue — on an easel, a stand, or mounted on foam board — and greets attendees with the loved one's name, dates, and a short message. It helps guests feel oriented and welcomed before they take a seat.
Unlike the folded program, which goes home with each person, the welcome sign stays at the venue. It works for traditional funerals, memorial services, and celebrations of life alike.
bullets: Shows the full name, birth and passing dates
Adds a brief phrase such as "Celebrating the Life of…" or "In Loving Memory"
Matches the visual theme of the program and memory cards for a cohesive look

sections.h2: What to write on a funeral welcome sign
paragraphs: Keep the text short so it reads clearly from a few feet away. Include the essentials first, then add one personal line if space allows.

Standard layout: full legal name (or the name they went by), birth year – passing year, service title ("Funeral Service," "Memorial Service," "Celebration of Life"), date and time of the service, and a short welcome line.
bullets: "Welcome to the Celebration of Life for Maria Elena Rossi"
"In Loving Memory of James T. Chen, 1952–2026"
"Please join us in remembering Sarah — Service begins at 2:00 PM"

sections.h2: Standard sizes and aspect ratios for printing
paragraphs: Most print shops and home printers handle a few common poster sizes. The 2:3 aspect ratio (24×36 in, 16×24 in, 12×18 in) scales cleanly without cropping. A 24×36 in sign is large enough for a chapel entrance; 16×24 in fits a tabletop easel; 12×18 in works for a smaller foyer.
If you design in a 2:3 ratio, you can print any of these three sizes from the same file — just choose the paper size at checkout.
bullets: 24×36 in — full easel sign, visible across a lobby
16×24 in — mid-size, easy to transport
12×18 in — compact, fits a small stand or table

sections.h2: How to personalize and print a welcome sign template
paragraphs: Open the fill-in PDF in the free Adobe Acrobat Reader app on your phone, tablet, or computer. Tap each placeholder — name, dates, service title, time — and type your text. Save the file. No design software, account, or subscription is needed.
Photos can be added on a computer only (drag and drop into the image frame). On a phone you can edit text but not insert images.

sections.h2: Printing at home vs. a local print shop
paragraphs: Home printing works if you have a printer that takes 11×17 in or 12×18 in paper and you're comfortable trimming. For 16×24 in or 24×36 in, a local shop is faster and cheaper than large-format inkjet ink. Most shops accept a PDF on a USB drive or emailed file and can mount on 3/16 in foam board while you wait.
Call ahead to confirm same-day turnaround and foam-board mounting; some locations need a few hours during peak times.
bullets: Home: 12×18 in on 65–80 lb matte cardstock, trim to size
Shop: 16×24 in or 24×36 in on matte poster paper + foam board mount
Bring the saved PDF on phone or USB; no account needed at the counter

faq.q: Can I edit the welcome sign on my phone?
faq.a: Yes. Open the PDF in the free Adobe Acrobat Reader app, tap the placeholder text, type your details, and save. Photo insertion works on a computer only.

faq.q: What paper weight should I use for a foam-board mounted sign?
faq.a: Ask the print shop for matte poster paper (typically 8–10 mil). They will spray-mount it to 3/16 in foam board so it stands rigid on an easel without curling.

faq.q: Does the template include bleed for edge-to-edge printing?
faq.a: The welcome sign file is set up at the exact trim size (24×36 in, 2:3 ratio). Most shops print with a small white border; if you need full bleed, ask them to print on 24.25×36.25 in and trim.

faq.q: Can I use the same template for a celebration of life instead of a funeral?
faq.a: Absolutely. Change the service title line to "Celebration of Life" or "Memorial Gathering" — the layout and botanical design work for any tone.

faq.q: How soon after purchase do I get the files?
faq.a: Instantly. The download link appears on the confirmation screen and is emailed to you. No account creation required.
